m:reichstag: The climb to the dome is free but you need to book on the Bundestag website, with your name and date of birth, and bring your original ID to the entrance; without a booking, when there's space, you can ask at the desk near the Berlin-Pavillon up to 2 hours ahead. The dome is closed for cleaning from 19 to 30 October (the roof terrace stays open).
m:linden: Free to walk around. The Humboldt Forum's courtyard and restaurant are open to everyone; the exhibitions are paid. Gendarmenmarkt square is especially beautiful at sunset.
m:museum: The Neues Museum, Altes Museum and Bode-Museum cost €14 each; the island day ticket costs €24. Hours: Tuesday–Sunday from 10am; the Neues Museum closes at 6pm, the Altes and Bode at 5pm (Tuesday–Friday) and 6pm (Saturday and Sunday). Closed on Mondays. The Pergamonmuseum is closed for restoration until 4 June 2027. Cathedral: Monday–Thursday 10am–6pm, Friday and Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday noon–5pm (hours stated on the website: check the price).
m:fernseh: Open every day from 9am to 11pm. The standard ticket starts from €20 (a «from» price on the website); booking online avoids the long queue. On 23 November 2026 the tower is closed.
m:mauer: The open-air exhibition is open every day from 8am to 10pm and the visitor centre and documentation centre are open Tuesday–Sunday 10am–6pm (last access to the tower 5:45pm), closed on Mondays. Entry is free. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December.
m:eastside: Free to walk along Mühlenstraße at any time. The stretch near Ostbahnhof is the busiest and the murals are being restored in turns: the quieter end is near the bridge.
m:potsdamer: The exhibition is free. Hours stated by guides: every day 10am–8pm (the outdoor part closes at sunset): check topographie.de. Checkpoint Charlie is a reconstruction with paid costumed actors: better to look at it from outside.
m:kreuz: On Thursdays from 5 to 10pm there's «Street Food Thursday» (the busiest evening). Small market Mon–Thu noon–6pm, big market Friday noon–6pm and Saturday 10am–6pm.
m:prenz: The Mauerpark flea market is usually on Sundays, about 10am–6pm (confirmed in guides: check before going).
m:tiergarten: The park is free and always open. The climb up the Victory Column is paid (about €4, not checked on the website: verify).
vd:bonanza: One of the specialty roasters that made Berlin's cafés famous: quality coffee and baked goods in a bright room in Prenzlauer Berg.
vp:bonanza: A coffee with a pastry is around €6–9 (menu not seen). Hours from the website.
vd:konnopke: The currywurst stand under the elevated U-Bahn since 1930, an institution of former East Berlin: sausage with curry sauce and chips, eaten standing under the yellow U2 line.
vp:konnopke: A currywurst with chips is usually around €6–8 (menu not seen). Closed Monday and Sunday.
vd:distrikt: Specialty coffee and a small Australian-style kitchen in Mitte, a few steps from Bernauer Straße: filter coffee, toast and cakes for an unhurried breakfast.
vp:distrikt: Breakfast with a coffee around €9–13 (menu not seen). Hours to be confirmed.
vd:vuong: A tiny Vietnamese kitchen in Mitte with a few stools: noodle soups, curries and rice with meat or tofu, cooked to order. One of Berliners' favourite places for a quick, tasty meal.
vp:vuong: A dish usually costs €9–13 (menu not seen). Hours to be confirmed and the place is small: there's a bit of a queue.
vd:barcomis: A historic Bergmannkiez café with American cheesecake and a good brunch: breakfasts, cakes and sandwiches in a shady courtyard.
vp:barcomis: Breakfast around €10–14 (menu not seen). Hours to be confirmed.
vd:markthalle: Kreuzberg's covered market with local producers, bakers and food stalls from around the world. On Thursday evenings (5–10pm) it becomes Street Food Thursday, with dozens of street food stalls.
vp:markthalle: A street food dish usually costs €7–12 (menu not seen). Hours from the hall's website; individual stalls open from around noon. On Sundays it's not open as a market (there's a children's market noon–4pm).
vd:curry36: Another historic currywurst stand, in Kreuzberg, open until 5am: the classic recipe with sausage (also vegetarian) and curry, eaten at the counter.
vp:curry36: A currywurst with chips is around €6–8 (menu not seen). Hours from the website: open every day from 9am to 5am the next day.
vd:mustafa: Berlin's most famous vegetable kebab stand: warm bread with chicken, roasted vegetables, feta and lemon. The queue is long at all hours, but it moves.
vp:mustafa: A kebab usually costs about €6–7 (menu not seen). Hours from guides: open until late at night; the queue is only worth it if you're not in a hurry.
vd:zurhenne: A Kreuzberg inn specialising in a single dish, roast chicken with potato salad and sauerkraut: the formula has been the same for over a hundred years, with prices still fair.
vp:zurhenne: Half a chicken with a side is around €12–15 (menu not seen). Hours from guides: closed on Mondays; best to book in the evening.
vd:datscha: A Russian-Ukrainian café in Friedrichshain, with a room full of vintage objects: big breakfasts, pelmeni, borscht and homemade cakes.
vp:datscha: A breakfast or a dish is usually under €14 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:neuensee: The beer garden on the Tiergarten lake: tables under the trees, pizza, Flammkuchen, German dishes and breakfasts. In autumn and winter you sit in the heated rooms.
vp:neuensee: A dish is usually around €12–16 (menu not seen). Hours from the website: open every day 9am–midnight.
cd:altesmuseum: Greek and Roman antiquities in the neoclassical museum on Museum Island.
cd:altenationalgalerie: Friedrich, Monet and Manet in a neoclassical temple on Museum Island.
cd:checkpoint: Stories of escapes from East Germany near the former checkpoint.
cd:ddr: Everyday life in East Germany: a hands-on museum, with a kitchen and a Trabant.
cd:jmb: Libeskind's museum: two thousand years of Jewish history in Germany.
cd:gemaldegalerie: European paintings from the 13th to the 18th century: Rembrandt, Vermeer, Raphael.
cd:hambahnhof: Contemporary art in a former railway station: Warhol and Beuys.
cd:charlottenburg: The Baroque palace of the Prussian kings, with state rooms and a garden to stroll in.
cd:dhm: Two thousand years of German history near Unter den Linden.
cd:stasi: The former headquarters of East Germany's secret police, with the minister's office.
cd:naturkunde: The big dinosaur skeleton and a collection of minerals and meteorites.
cd:spreefahrt: An hour on the river past Museum Island, the Reichstag and the Chancellery.
